theorem.justification: The pair of observation experiments proves that scalar summaries cannot decide strict nonconcurrent-control gain when realized propensities may encode omitted outcomes.
theorem.gap: The result rules out the requested four-scalar necessary-and-sufficient criterion on the general continuous adaptive class without substituting an AIPW optimality condition.
theorem.consumer: A full-record versus concurrent-record comparison must retain the information map carried by realized propensity vectors.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof uses sequential randomization to convert predictable propensities into assignment probabilities, window availability to apply the floor to the control arm, and product-prior admissibility to average uniform honesty over the prior; these load-bearing dependencies were omitted.

proposed.justification: Multiplying posterior coverage by missing squared-weight mass spends the global error budget once and preserves the linear phase margin.
proposed.gap: Standard two-prior testing bounds can be zero when \(\alpha<p_{\mathrm{floor}}\le2\alpha\); the weighted posterior calculation remains positive throughout the full strict phase.
proposed.consumer: The lemma lower-bounds every randomized variable-length interval, including procedures unrelated to AIPW.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof directly invokes the control total-variation restriction to bound estimator bias and the target-weight-scale definition to evaluate concurrent weights; these dependencies were omitted.

proposed.justification: Concurrent weights eliminate drift bias and put the constructive radius on the same target-weight scale as the all-kernel lower bound.
proposed.gap: The claim is finite-population, finite-horizon, bias-aware, and evaluated against an unrestricted minimax criterion.
proposed.consumer: A platform-trial analysis can compute \(I^\star\) and attach a design-certified worst-case expected-length guarantee without regression consistency.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The exact calculation directly uses the sequential assignment law, the bounded-TV schedule family and causal target, and the drift, variance, and optimized-radius constructions; these load-bearing dependencies were omitted.

proposed.justification: The exact continuous experiment proves both necessity of the strict phase and a genuine all-kernel nonconcurrent-control borrowing criterion in a legal platform family.
proposed.gap: The proposition settles the continuum coefficient and optimizes over variable-length confidence procedures.
proposed.consumer: The one-unit formula is a calibration and unit-test benchmark for numerical primal--dual solvers used in platform-trial sensitivity analysis.
